propositions: Upper-bound wall-clock assertions in tests cause CI flakiness under runner contention; detector must block new unescaped instances in tests/** with teaching message naming both valid escapes.

Two high-frequency test sites (test_config_perf.py:201 and test_enrich_drain.py:261) require migration from timing assertions to counting-proxy spies (config._ordered_layers and pending_enrichment respectively) to avoid cache/drain path regression.
Eleven remaining in-scope test sites with upper-bound wall-clock assertions require '# timing: hang-guard — <reason>' markers documenting their hang-guard necessity.

Detector must recognize and permit two escape mechanisms: the '# timing: hang-guard' line marker and the '@pytest.mark.skipif(os.environ.get("CI"))' perf-lane guard; bare '@pytest.mark.benchmark' without skipif does NOT escape.

Detector unit tests must cover fire cases (elapsed, monotonic subtraction, multiline), both escape paths, marker-without-reason rejection, lower-bound exclusion, and self-exclusion via EXCLUDED_FILES.
